title: Finite-level degree-one Poincare pairing on a curve
statement:
Let $C_0/k_0$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve,
let $C=C_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$, and put
$A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ with
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$. The cup product followed by the
trace gives a perfect $A_n$-bilinear pairing

$$
H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C,A_n)\times
H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C,A_n(1))\longrightarrow A_n.
\tag{3.4}
$$

Here the coefficient and twist conventions are those of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text:
Put $R=A_n$. Write $
u_C:C_{\mathrm{proet}}	o C_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison and put $L=R\Gamma(C,A_n(1))$, derived global sections on the pro-etale site with the twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. By [lem-wf-curve-kummer-jacobian-tate-module], $A_n(1)$ is canonically $
u_C^*\mu_{\ell^n,C}$, and $
u_C^*$ of the etale constant sheaf $A_n$ is the pro-etale constant sheaf $A_n$; hence [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] identifies $H^i(L)$ with $H^i_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C,\mu_{\ell^n})$ and $H^i(R\Gamma(C,A_n))$ with $H^i_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(C,A_n)$ for every $i$, and the etale groups in (3.4) are these pro-etale groups. The curve $C$ is smooth, separated, and connected over the algebraically closed field $\overline{k}_0$, so [lem-sc-cohomological-dimension] gives $H^i(L)=0$ for $i>2$; because $L$ is derived global sections of a sheaf in degree zero, its negative cohomology also vanishes. Connectedness and the primitive-root trivialization identify $H^0(L)$ with $R(1)$. Under the same trivialization, [thm-sc-proper-cohomology] gives $H^2(L)\cong R$, free of rank one. The Kummer/Jacobian isomorphism of [lem-wf-curve-kummer-jacobian-tate-module], followed by [thm-av-final](c), gives $H^1(L)\cong J[\ell^n](\overline{k}_0)\cong R^{2g}$, where $g=\dim J$. Thus all cohomology modules of $L$ are finite free. Choosing a primitive $\ell^n$-th root also gives a noncanonical sheaf isomorphism $A_n(1)\cong A_n$, so the cohomology modules of $R\Gamma(C,A_n)$ are finite free.

By [thm-pod-point-perfectness], both $L$ and $R\Gamma(C,A_n)$ admit bounded finite-free models. Apply [lem-wf-bounded-free-complex-projective-cohomology-splitting] to each model, since Step 1 gives projective (indeed finite free) cohomology, to obtain in the derived category the direct-sum decompositions $L\simeq\bigoplus_iH^i(L)[-i]$ and $R\Gamma(C,A_n)\simeq\bigoplus_iH^i(C,A_n)[-i]$.

Here $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $\overline{k}_0=k$ are the global finite-field datum of the blueprint, so with $X_0=C_0$, $d=1$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ we are in the fixed setting of [def-pod-conventions]: $C_0$ is smooth, separated of finite type, geometrically connected and of pure dimension one, and $X=C$. Specialize [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality] to the proper curve $C$ (properness of $C_0$ is its extra hypothesis), the constant coefficient object $K=A_n$, and $d=1$. The constant coefficient object is free of rank one and hence perfect, while its coefficient dual $R\mathcal Hom(A_n,A_n)=A_n$ with the degree-one twist is $A_n(1)$ by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The theorem identifies the derived dual with the twisted complex:
$$R\Gamma(C,A_n)^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}L[2],$$
with inverse the adjoint of the derived pairing $\beta_{A_n}$.

By Step 2, $R\Gamma(C,A_n)\simeq\bigoplus_iH^i(C,A_n)[-i]$ with finite free summands, so $R\Gamma(C,A_n)^\vee\simeq\bigoplus_iH^i(C,A_n)^\vee[i]$ and $H^{-1}(R\Gamma(C,A_n)^\vee)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(H^1(C,A_n),A_n)$; on the other side $H^{-1}(L[2])=H^1(L)$. Taking $H^{-1}$ of the isomorphism in Step 3 therefore yields
$$H^1(C,A_n(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(C,A_n)^\vee.$$
By [prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing] the degree-zero part of $\beta_{A_n}$, read through the proper comparison $R\Gamma_c=R\Gamma$ of [thm-pod-proper-poincare-duality], is the pairing $\langle x,y\rangle_1$ on $H^1(C,A_n)\times H^1(C,A_n(1))$, namely cup product, evaluation $A_n\otimes A_n(1)\to A_n(1)$, and the normalized smooth trace $\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}:H^2(C,A_n(1))\to A_n$. Hence the displayed map is $y\mapsto\langle-,y\rangle_1$, the adjoint of the cup–trace pairing. The same computation in degree $-2$ (where $H^0(C,A_n)=A_n$ by connectedness) shows that $y\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}(y)$ is an isomorphism $H^2(C,A_n(1))\to A_n$.

The adjoint of Step 4 is an isomorphism of $A_n$-modules, so the cup–trace pairing (3.4) is perfect over $A_n$. The conclusion does not depend on the normalization of the trace: any $A_n$-linear isomorphism $t:H^2(C,A_n(1))\to A_n$ satisfies $t=u\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}$ with $u=t\circ(\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}})^{-1}(1)\in A_n^\times$, and multiplying a perfect pairing by a unit leaves it perfect. Its Frobenius equivariance (not needed for perfectness) is the finite-level specialization of [thm-pod-equivariance-of-the-twisted-pairing].

split_report.summary: Audited the imported finite-level Poincare pairing against the current main-20261015 blueprint and the cited DAG statements. No exact sorry-free Lean declaration exists. The first proof step verifies the finite-free cohomology of the twisted and untwisted complexes from curve cohomological dimension, the proper-curve Kummer computation, the Kummer/Jacobian identification, and abelian-variety torsion. The second step factors the point-perfectness finite-free models through one new statement-only splitting lemma for bounded finite-free complexes with projective cohomology. Proper derived duality then gives the degree-one adjoint, which is the cup-trace pairing; the final step records the existing equivariance consequence. The item statement is unchanged. Maintainer reader (2026-10-18): steps 1 and 4 now cite the etale/pro-etale cohomology comparison explicitly, step 3 checks the fixed setting of def-pod-conventions, step 4 cites prop-pod-degree-of-the-pairing for the degree-one pairing, step 5 notes independence of the trace normalization, and the off-route use of thm-pod-point-perfectness is declared.

lean.statement: theorem exists_curveFiniteLevel_perfectPairing (k₀ K : Type u) [Field k₀] [Field K] [Algebra k₀ K] [IsAlgClosure k₀ K] [IsAlgClosed K] (C₀ : Scheme.{u}) [C₀.Over (Spec (.of k₀))] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C₀ ↘ Spec (.of k₀))] [IsProjective (C₀ ↘ Spec (.of k₀))] [GeometricallyConnected (C₀ ↘ Spec (.of k₀))] (C : Scheme.{u}) [C.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsConnectedCurve (C ↘ Spec (.of K))] [Smooth (C ↘ Spec (.of K))] [IsProper (C ↘ Spec (.of K))] (p : C ⟶ C₀) (hC : IsPullback p (C ↘ Spec (.of K)) (C₀ ↘ Spec (.of k₀)) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k₀ K)))) (ell c : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] [CharP k₀ c] [CharP K c] (hell : ell ≠ c) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : ∃ (m : Module (ZMod (ell ^ n)) (Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod (ell ^ n)) 1)) (m' : Module (ZMod (ell ^ n)) (Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (ell ^ n)) 1)), ((fun [m₁ : Module (ZMod (ell ^ n)) (Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod (ell ^ n)) 1)] [m₂ : Module (ZMod (ell ^ n)) (Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (ell ^ n)) 1)] => ∃ B : Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod (ell ^ n)) 1 →ₗ[ZMod (ell ^ n)] Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (ell ^ n)) 1 →ₗ[ZMod (ell ^ n)] ZMod (ell ^ n), (∀ (x : Sheaf.H (C.constantZMod (ell ^ n)) 1) (y : Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (ell ^ n)) 1), B x y = Scheme.degreeNormalizedCurveTrace K C (C ↘ Spec (.of K)) ell c hell n hn (C.finiteCoefficientCup (ell ^ n) 1 1 2 rfl x y)) ∧ B.IsPerfPair) (m₁ := m) (m₂ := m'))
lean.note: Uses the published finite coefficient cup and unique degree-normalized trace. Existential module structures supply the unique ZMod actions on ordinary Sheaf.H without extra scalar-action hypotheses; IsPerfPair states bijectivity of both linear adjoints.
